$comment: Third-party images mirrored into PRIVATE ECR for step 10 (Argo CD coexistence).
WHY A MIRROR EXISTS AT ALL. The node groups sit in fully-isolated subnets with no
NAT and no internet gateway (a deliberate earlier decision). Pods can therefore
only pull from private ECR, reached over the ECR interface endpoints and the S3
gateway endpoint created in step 3a.
public.ecr.aws IS NOT A SHORTCUT. Argo CD's own manifest pulls its cache (redis) from
public.ecr.aws, which looks like it might already work from a private subnet. It
does not: the ECR interface endpoints (api.ecr / dkr.ecr) serve PRIVATE ECR only.
ECR Public is a separate, internet-facing service. The cache image must be mirrored
like everything else -- and it is mirrored as VALKEY, not Redis: see that entry's
note for the license reason and the compatibility evidence.
PINNED BY DIGEST, NOT BY TAG. Tags upstream are mutable, so a tag-only mirror is
neither reproducible nor verifiable. TWO digests are pinned per image:
digest      - the multi-platform INDEX digest
arm64Digest - the linux/arm64 child manifest digest inside that index
The mirror copies only linux/arm64 by default and verifies arm64Digest after the
push; MIRROR_FULL_INDEX=true copies the whole index and verifies `digest`. Both
modes are therefore verifiable -- the pushed image is read back from ECR and its
digest compared against what was reviewed here.
WHY ARM64-ONLY IS THE DEFAULT, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED. Summing the layer bytes of
every child manifest on 2026-08-25: a full-index mirror of these five images moves
1500 MB per region (3000 MB across both), against 309 MB per region (619 MB) for
linux/arm64 alone -- 4.8x the data. The surplus is amd64, 386, ppc64le, s390x,
arm/v6, arm/v7 and riscv64, none of which this node group can run. Flattening also
sidesteps the attestation manifests that nginx carries (8 entries
with architecture "unknown"; the valkey index carries none), which are a known
source of ECR push friction.
EVERY DIGEST BELOW WAS RESOLVED FROM THE LIVE REGISTRY on 2026-08-25 and every
image was confirmed to publish linux/arm64 -- the node group is
AL2023_ARM_64_STANDARD on m7g (Graviton). An image lacking arm64 schedules and
then CrashLoopBackOffs with 'exec format error', which reads as an application
fault rather than a platform mismatch.
THE IMAGE LIST IS DERIVED, NOT GUESSED. It comes from the upstream install
manifests for the pinned versions:
argo-cd      manifests/install.yaml at v3.4.9   -> argocd, redis (served by valkey); its dex objects are dropped by src/argo/render.sh (no SSO configured)
metrics-server components.yaml at v0.9.0        -> metrics-server
One argocd image backs FIVE workloads (server, repo-server,
application-controller, applicationset-controller, notifications-controller), so
the list is much shorter than the workload count suggests.
To re-pin: bump tag, re-resolve the digest from the registry, re-confirm arm64,
and re-read the upstream install manifest in case the component images changed.

images.name: argocd
images.note: Backs argocd-server, repo-server, application-controller, applicationset-controller and notifications-controller. v3.4.9 chosen over v3.5.3: last patch of the previous minor, so it carries nine patches of field exposure rather than three. Re-pinned from v3.4.7 on 2026-09-28 to clear Amazon Inspector findings: v3.4.9's install.yaml differs from v3.4.7's only in the argocd image tag, and a linux/arm64 scan shows 45 fewer CVE ids with none added. Digests resolved from quay.io 2026-09-28 and cross-checked as the sha256 of the manifest bytes. An Argo failure on stage would look like the very conflict this demo disproves.

images.name: valkey
images.note: Serves the cache that argo-cd v3.4.9's install.yaml names as redis:8.2.3-alpine. Redis 8 is licensed RSALv2 / SSPLv1 / AGPLv3, none of them a permissive license; Valkey is the Linux Foundation fork of the BSD-3-Clause Redis 7.2 codebase and speaks the same protocol, and Argo CD uses the cache only through standard commands (its repo-server and application-controller hold no Redis-8-only features). src/argo/render.sh repoints the manifest's redis reference at this entry; the image ships redis-server/redis-cli compatibility names and the same uid 999 the Deployment runs as. 9.0.6 chosen over 9.1.x for the same reason as argocd: last patch of the previous minor. Digest COMPUTED as sha256 of the manifest bytes (ECR Public returns no docker-content-digest header) and cross-checked 2026-09-17 against Docker Hub's header for the same tag -- identical.

images.name: metrics-server
images.note: Hard prerequisite for the HPA: an HPA cannot read CPU without it, so with metrics-server absent the HPA reports <unknown>/target and never acts -- which would silently remove the third controller the coexistence story depends on.

images.name: nginx
images.note: Serves the packaged Helm chart plus index.yaml in-cluster. Argo CD accepts git, http Helm and OCI sources; ECR-as-OCI was rejected because its auth token expires after 12 hours (see plan step 10). Digest computed the same way as valkey.

images.name: karpenter-controller
images.note: Karpenter node autoscaler (step 11, Option C: baseline capacity on the managed node group, surge provisioned by Karpenter). Karpenter's own docs require the image be copied into private ECR for a private cluster -- pulling from public.ecr.aws fails there, and the reported symptom is an image-pull timeout that reads as a network fault. Version 1.14.1 against a pinned Kubernetes 1.36: the compatibility matrix requires >= 1.13 for 1.36 (checked 2026-09-21), so 1.14.1 clears the floor with one minor to spare. Re-check that matrix on any Kubernetes version bump.

images.name: aws-load-balancer-controller
images.note: AWS Load Balancer Controller. Replaces the in-tree service controller so the app NLB gets ip targets, cross-zone load balancing and ARC zonal shift -- none of which the in-tree controller can enable, and without which a zonal shift reports ACTIVE and moves nothing measurable. Runs IN-CLUSTER (unlike the in-tree controller, which runs on the AWS-managed control plane), so it needs both this mirror and the elasticloadbalancing VPC endpoint. Re-pinned from v3.5.0 on 2026-10-06 to clear the 8 Amazon Inspector findings against v3.5.0 (1 critical, 5 high). There is no v3.5.x patch, so the fix is the next minor, released 2026-10-05: fresher than the argocd and valkey rule of taking the previous minor's last patch, and taken anyway because its changes sit in Gateway API, cross-account TargetGroupBinding and Ingress features this service does not use (it runs one NLB Service), and its upstream IAM policy is byte-identical to v3.5.0's. Digests resolved from the live registry 2026-10-06, the index digest cross-checked as the sha256 of the manifest bytes; publishes linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 only. Chart 3.6.0 -> appVersion v3.6.0; tag and arm64Digest must equal IMAGE_TAG and IMAGE_DIGEST in src/lbc/render.sh, asserted by a test.

images.name: aws-for-fluent-bit
images.note: Cluster-wide pod log shipper (k8s/fluent-bit.yaml). Runs IN-CLUSTER on nodes in isolated subnets with NO NAT, so public.ecr.aws is unreachable at runtime and this mirror is mandatory rather than an optimisation -- reachability to CloudWatch Logs comes from the pre-existing CLOUDWATCH_LOGS interface endpoint. Re-pinned 2026-09-28 from 2.34.3 to the dated rebuild 2.34.3.20260918 (the digest the `stable` tag points at that day): same Fluent Bit 1.9.10, with the Go plugins rebuilt on go1.27.1 and the Amazon Linux 2 packages refreshed, clearing Amazon Inspector findings against 2.34.3 (go/stdlib 1.25.5, openssl, python, vim). The 2.34.x line is still Amazon Linux 2, so Inspector's end-of-support finding for that base remains until a 3.x (Amazon Linux 2023) migration. Digests resolved from the live registry 2026-09-28: the index digest was computed as the sha256 of the manifest-list bytes because public.ecr.aws returns no Docker-Content-Digest header for this repo, which is authoritative since a manifest digest IS the hash of those bytes. Publishes linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 only. arm64Digest is the CHILD manifest and is what the manifest references (docs/lessons.md #10: the arm64-only copy means the INDEX digest never lands in ECR, so referencing it fails as a pull timeout that reads like a network fault). tag and arm64Digest must equal the image line in k8s/fluent-bit.yaml -- asserted by a test.
